questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(6,0),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=3,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=6.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-6)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{(y-0)^{2}}{{6}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-6)^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{36} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

For the ellipse $\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{18}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16}=1,$ find the lengths of its major and minor axes.

$\,$ The length of the major axis is 
{{field-1}}.

questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

In the given equation, we have $h=2$ and $k=-1,$ so the center is located at $(2,-1).$

In the given equation, we also have ${a}^{2}=18$ and ${b}^{2}=16.$

- Since ${a}^{2}=18,$ the length of the horizontal radius must be $a=\sqrt{18}=3\sqrt{2}.$

- Since ${b}^{2}=16,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{16}=4.$

So the semi-major axis has length $a=3\sqrt{2},$ and the semi-minor axis has length $b=4.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2a=2\cdot 3\sqrt{2}=6\sqrt{2},$ and the minor axis has length $2b=2\cdot 4=8.$
